spots.d: Plants, craft beer and a tiny concert room in a former chemical factory. The reaction is now mostly social.
Big terrace, small square, sits on the site of the original Lumen. Summer save point.

spots.a: Bródy Sándor utca, start of the street
spots.d: A beer institute by the Museum Garden. Several taps, one terrace, full of students researching.
A university cellar pub open to everyone. Drinks only after 16:00, so finish your thesis first.
Living-room bar with craft beer and cocktails. Like a mate's flat if your mate could mix.
Craft beer spot loved by locals. Do not release it.
Full name: Fővárosi Kulipintyó. A small local pub with no interest in your brunch plans.
Feels less like a pub, more like a dorm club that forgot to close.
Cooperative-run community house: gigs, film nights, rooftop terrace. Owned by the people pouring your beer.
Bar, gig room and NGO hive. Has survived more closure orders than any other final boss on this map.
Huge pub with swings, many rooms and a mulberry tree the owners rescued from the chop.
Café, gallery and analogue photo hub in a former flat. Develops film and regrettable friendships.
Bookshop plus gallery. Two reasons to stand around looking thoughtful.
Gallery in the Palace Quarter, on the same street as half your coffee options.
Ceramics workshop. Drink specialty coffee from a cup you made, leak included.
Local history in the rooms of the legendary Józsefvárosi Kiállítóterem, an art venue from 1976 to 1988.
Community house where an alliance of social and cultural groups share one roof and one boiler-sized idea.
Specialty coffee and toasties by day. Turns into a bar on Friday and Saturday nights.
Moved exactly one door over and got bigger. The shortest relocation in district history.

spots.a: Bródy Sándor utca, near Gutenberg tér
spots.d: Own pastries, own sourdough. Arrive early, leave heavier.
Student HQ with a daily lunch menu. Group projects go here to die.
Market hall from 1897 with hot food counters and Saturday chaos. Still open after everything that happened around it.
Where the old market traders moved. Go hungry and follow the people who know.
One of the biggest vintage floors around. Bring a free afternoon and low standards for fitting rooms.
Eclectic vintage for people who think matching is a weakness.
Clothes and accessories behind the market hall. Short opening hours, so treat it like a rare spawn.
Carefully curated second hand for all. No typos detected.
Small shop, big rack of women's clothing. Do not feed after midnight.
The square held the city's official junk market from 1897 to 1950. The Teleki Zsibi flea market keeps the sport alive.
A working public library inside the Wenckheim Palace. Revise in a ballroom like the aristocrat you are not.
Square that hosts the winter Térvarázs. Once featured metal samba. Yes, metal samba.
Park at the heart of the Magdolna Quarter, and stage of the Night of Gypsy Music.
The botanic garden. Secret green level hidden behind the blocks.
The biggest quiet zone on the map. Very low noise complaints.
A parked car dropped into a pit about 2.5 m wide and 6-7 m long. By 2016 residents were saying the street was under siege from utility works. Do not park on this tile.
spots.n: The Street That Ate A Car

spots.d: Police searched Auróra for 14 hours, detained 15 people and also seized industrial hemp from a sustainability programme. A closure order followed in 2018; the place opened the next day anyway. In 2019 police were the surprise guests at a fundraiser.
A 39,000 m2 container market with over 2,000 stall tenants at its peak, running since 1993. Bailiffs and police cleared it. Traders crossed the road and the game continued.

spots.a: Blaha Lujza tér, on the department store roof
spots.d: Rooftop terrace on the fifth floor from May 2007. Closed by the district in 2018. Game over, no continues.
The rebuild took 505 days and 3.68 billion forints, adding 80 trees to the ten already there. People took the square back with tea and frantic dancing on opening day.
Rising rents pushed Gólya out of its old pub. It crowdfunded a building of its own, renovated largely by volunteers. Gentrification: 1, Storks: still flying.
The Grund Kert community garden was cleared for new Corvin Sétány housing. HVG reported a huge hole where one of the most colourful corners had been.
No joke on this one. After days stranded outside a closed station, about a thousand people, mostly Syrians, set off from here on foot for Vienna.
